title: Joshua 17
paragraphs: ¹ The allotment was made for the tribe of Manasseh, Joseph's firstborn. Machir, Manasseh's firstborn and the father of Gilead, was a warrior, so Gilead and Bashan were given to him. ² The remaining descendants of Manasseh received allotments by their clans — the families of Abiezer, Helek, Asriel, Shechem, Hepher, and Shemida. These were the male descendants of Manasseh son of Joseph by their clans. ³ Now Zelophehad son of Hepher, the son of Gilead, the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh, had no sons, only daughters. Their names were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah. ⁴ They came before Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun and the leaders, saying, The LORD commanded Moses to give us an inheritance among our male relatives. So in accordance with the LORD's command, Joshua gave them an inheritance among their father's brothers. ⁵ Manasseh received ten shares of land, in addition to the lands of Gilead and Bashan east of the Jordan,

⁶ because Manasseh's daughters received an inheritance along with his sons. The land of Gilead went to the rest of Manasseh's sons. ⁷ The territory of Manasseh ran from Asher to Michmethath near Shechem. The boundary ran southward from there to the inhabitants of En Tappuah. ⁸ Manasseh had the land of Tappuah, but the town of Tappuah on the border of Manasseh belonged to the Ephraimites. ⁹ The boundary then went down to the Kanah Ravine. The towns south of the ravine belonged to Ephraim, though they were within the territory of Manasseh. The border of Manasseh ran along the north side of the ravine and ended at the sea. ¹⁰ The land to the south belonged to Ephraim and the land to the north belonged to Manasseh, with the sea as the western border. The two tribes met in Asher on the north and Issachar on the east.

¹¹ Within Issachar and Asher, Manasseh also had Beth Shean and its surrounding settlements, Ibleam and its settlements, and the inhabitants of Dor, En Dor, Taanach, and Megiddo, along with their settlements — three hill districts. ¹² Yet the Manassites were unable to drive out the inhabitants of those towns, and the Canaanites were determined to stay in that region. ¹³ When the Israelites grew stronger, they subjected the Canaanites to forced labor but did not drive them out completely. ¹⁴ The descendants of Joseph complained to Joshua, Why have you given us only one allotment and one portion as our inheritance? We are a numerous people, for the LORD has blessed us greatly. ¹⁵ Joshua answered, If you are so numerous and the hill country of Ephraim is not big enough for you, go up into the forest and clear land for yourself in the territory of the Perizzites and Rephaites.

¹⁶ The descendants of Joseph replied, The hill country is not enough for us, and the Canaanites living in the valley all have iron chariots — both those in Beth Shean and its settlements and those in the Valley of Jezreel. ¹⁷ But Joshua said to the tribes of Joseph — to Ephraim and Manasseh — You are a numerous people and you have great power. You will not have just one allotment. ¹⁸ The forested hill country will be yours as well. Though it is heavily wooded, clear it and its farthest limits will be yours. Even though the Canaanites have iron chariots and are strong, you can drive them out.
